item.title: [LU-20723] reduce Autotest configs to fewer VMs under load
item.description:
It turns out that most test scripts do not use the second client during any tests, so having an extra VM configured for those scripts is just wasted resources. This can be seen by checking for (the lack of) CLIENTS, CLIENT2 and CLIENTCOUNT usage in the test scripts.

By consolidating test scripts that need multiple clients into a single test session and reducing the remaining sessions from 5 VMs to 4 (client, 2x MDS, OSS), there could be 25% more sessions running on the same hardware.

The test scripts that use CLIENTS, CLIENT2 and SINGLEAGT in a non-trivial manner and need to run with 5 VMs:

  • large-scale.sh, recovery-{double,mds,oss,random}-scale.sh check $CLIENTCOUNT at the start and refuse to run otherwise. I don't think these are run during review sessions.
  • sanity-hsm.sh, sanity-pcc.sh depend on SINGLEAGT (usually CLIENT2) to run a separate HSM data transfer agent. I don't know if that could be changed to use $MOUNT2 on the same node, but is not "low hanging fruit"

These scripts prefer to have CLIENT2 but could live without it for most subtests, and should run with 5 VMs if available:

  • recovery-small.sh, replay-dual.sh, replay-vbr.sh - use CLIENT2 when available, or fall back to MOUNT2 but then some subtests are skipped entirely
  • parallel-scale-nfs*.sh use LUSTRE_CLIENT_NFSSRV (defaults to the MDS, not sure if Autotest puts it on CLIENT2), and NFS_CLIENTS=CLIENTS so does not actually require an additional client, but may benefit from one if that is how Autotest has previously been running it, otherwise it could go into the "never need second client VM" group

These scripts use CLIENTS, CLIENT2 in a passing manner and never need a second client VM, or could easily be fixed to avoid it entirely:

  • replay-single.sh has a few subtests that use which could move into replay-dual.sh
  • sanity.sh and sanityn.sh have a few subtests that can optionally use CLIENT2, and only sanity.sh test_160v and sanityn.sh test_33[abc] *require* a second client and can very likely be changed to use MOUNT2 instead
  • the remaining scripts do not have any visible usage of additional client(s), though it is possible that is done in some other manner.

It would also be possible to run (some? all?) review-dne-part-N sessions with a 1-MDS DNE configuration with 2-MDT (or 4-MDT) on the one MDS instead of 2-MDS 4-MDTs used today, which could reduce the test cluster size to 3 VMs under congestion. I don't know if that would cause some other test fallout (due to hidden test assumptions) but it could be used to further decrease test resources under high demand. Probably 1-MDS 2-MDT is enough for most cases, and I see only 3 subtests that *require* MDSCOUNT >= 3, and the rest will just optionally use more.

Preferably, the review-dne-part-N sessions would run with 2-MDS 4-MDT configs when there is no (big) test queue, and drop to 1-MDS 2-MDT (or 1-MDS 4-MDT if it passes or is fixed) testing when there is a (big) backlog.
item.summary: reduce Autotest configs to fewer VMs under load

status.description: This issue is being actively worked on at the moment by the assignee.

comments.comment:
green, mvef, colmstea, please provide your feedback on this.

My suggestion would be to first reorder the test scripts between review-dne-part-N as needed, if that can be done transparently. Then trigger a few test test sessions on existing patches explicitly using new config(s) (e.g. Test-Parameters: clientcount=1 mdscount=1 mdtcount=2) to confirm they are passing, and then roll out incrementally between Onyx and Trevis as new sessions are started (if that is possible).

If getting load-demand functionality would delay the rollout, then it seems like going to a smaller static config for a few days would get us out of the current backlog and allow more time to get a load-based configuration implemented and tested.

Thanks Andreas. I've looked into restructuring the -part-N sessions based on what each test needs (Claude helped with this because of the sheer number of tests). I also included Janitor, which runs single-client tests and is an indicator of which tests work on a single client.

Some notes first: (1) Of the existing groups, only part-3 (conf-sanity) could go to a single client without skipping anything, so the other groups need restructuring first. Also, a few statistics/reports use testgroups in Maloo. So, those would break after such a restructuring. (2) To clarify for sanity-hsm and sanity-pcc: The HSM agent can run locally (see test-framework.sh - init_agt_vars(). When no remote client is available, the copytool is started on the local client instead. However, several tests still need two clients either way, so we can't just move them to a single client.

Here is a possible proposal with estimated runtimes and how many VMs we'd save:

New groups

new group VMs suites runtime subtests that need 2 clients
part-1 4 sanity 4.7 h 160v skips
part-2 4 sanityn, sanity-lfsck, sanity-pfl, sanity-lnet, pjdfstest, runtests, sanity-ec (master mod), lnet-selftest, mds-survey 5.1 h sanityn 33b skips (cross-node benchmark, 33a already SLOW-only)
part-3 4 conf-sanity 7.2 h (zfs sample) none
part-4 5 sanity-sec, sanity-pcc, sanity-hsm 3.8 h sanity-sec 23a, 23b, 75a, 81b (nodemap/banlist by client NID), 48b; sanity-hsm 12h, 30a, 30b, 30c, 57, 256; sanity-pcc 2b
part-5 5 recovery-small, insanity, replay-dual, large-scale 4.1 h recovery-small 10e, 17b, 105, 134; replay-dual 21b, 29; insanity 3, 11-14 (client failure steps no-op without remote clients); large-scale entirely
part-6 4 replay-single, replay-vbr, ost-pools 4.0 h replay-single 70a, 200 and replay-vbr 10b skip
part-7 4 sanity-quota, sanity-scrub, sanity-flr, sanity-dom, lustre-rsync-test, replay-ost-single, mmp 4.8 h none
part-8   removed: replay-dual currently runs in both part-2 and part-8, replay-vbr moves to part-6    
part-9 5 unchanged: parallel-scale, parallel-scale-nfsv3/v4, performance-sanity, racer, obdfilter-survey, sanity-benchmark non-enforced multi-client workloads by design

Note: With this layout, the only two-client subtests no longer run in review are sanity 160v, sanityn 33b, replay-single 70a/200, and replay-vbr 10b; they stay covered by the full-* sessions as long as those keep two clients. We could also move these subtests into the two-client suites (which unfortunately will break Maloo statistics).

VM savings

scope today after saved
per distro, parts 1-8 8 groups, 40 VMs 7 groups, 30 VMs 10 VMs, 25%
per master patch, 46 enforced sessions (39 DNE, 7 non-DNE) ~223 VMs ~173 VMs 40-50 VMs, 18-22%

Assumptions behind the savings row: Autotest's clientcount default is 2 (no review base in autotest_configs sets it), and non-DNE sessions are 4 VMs today (one MDS). It is a range because not all distros run the same set, e.g., el9.8 and el10.1 subsets enforce part-8 but not part-5.

This is the theory: I'll push a patch to confirm the proposal.

Except for the couple of tests that need 2 clients (see the last column in the table above totalling 5 tests), the tests ran correctly with only one client. It seems worth to move these 5 tests into another testlist so they still run for each patch but allow freeing up VM resources.

In summary: Such a restructuring is possible, and the table gives a good overview of which test lists can run with one client.

My suggestion would be to first reorder the test scripts between review-dne-part-N as needed, if that can be done transparently.

The test configs are versioned and each Jenkins build is related to the version it is tested against so re-ordering test groups will not impact builds built before the re-ordering.

and then roll out incrementally between Onyx and Trevis as new sessions are started (if that is possible).

The test configs are global, once a new version is pushed it is picked up by onyx and trevis.

 

If getting load-demand functionality would delay the rollout, then it seems like going to a smaller static config for a few days would get us out of the current backlog and allow more time to get a load-based configuration implemented and tested.

probably test_278 could be tuned to run with less space, but not the others.  I'm generally OK with reducing the test coverage in these cases to get more test throughput.

colmstea, could https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_matrix (or a new page) be expanded to show the current mapping of test sessions to the test scripts that are run, or possibly autotest-config (IIRC) be made available read-only? I find that the LLMs are repeatedly adding test sessions like Test-Parameters: testlist=sanity env=ONLY=123 because that subtest was added/modified, but they are totally useless in the face of trivial and regular test sessions running sanity multiple times already, and subtest-change is running the changed subtest in a loop... Those sessions add the 30 minute provisioning/initialization steps, then run for 2s of "useful" time. If the test_matrix and test script mapping is referenced from the Lustre .agents/skills/lustre-test-scripts then they can make a better decision on what scripts to run (if any).

So review-dne test group tests are most of our testing, about 80% of the time per patch, and all run on two server distros. While we need to cover both distros, repeating everything catches almost no bugs but is really expensive. We could instead run half of the groups on one distro and half on the other. This would still get us plenty of distro-specific exposure but drop our autotest cost per patch by 40%.

Note a recent change: There are 17 groups overall, and until November 3 we only ran 9 of them twice. As of November 3rd, we run all 17 twice. That increased our cost per patch by almost 30%, which makes things much worse.

mvef sebastien green fyi on the distro suggestion above - I know we've got a severe backlog in autotest right now, and this splitting would help enormously.  (Removing 40% of all test time)

Also note the recent change to double up a bunch more suites which made things even more expensive.

I agree that running double testing is not worthwhile for the marginal improvement in coverage. Yes, there are some subtests that fail for specific distros (e.g. bugs in page cache or other VFS interfaces, or changes in the kernel APIs), but that is pretty rare. Alternating the distro/fstype like that gives good coverage to both distros for every test case.

I wouldn't be against randomizing the combinations even more to get better coverage (e.g. conf-sanity with ubuntu2604 servers), so long as PW catches the "consistent intermittent" failures and points them out (ideally also developing and landing the fix while we drink beer on the beach...). See my ideas in https://review.whamcloud.com/70263 ("LU-20869 tests: test one upgrade image per conf-sanity 32a-d").

I agree with Patrick and Andreas. Alternating distro and fstype seems reasonable. Unfortunately, the other change undid some of the efforts here and worsened the situation.

colmstea are you able to look into this and update the test config accordingly?
